test: A plan with one requires edge to a merged ticket outside the epic: the gate passes it and the lane starts with no refusal. Asking for the assembly working copy twice after a child has landed keeps that child's commit.

what: tea-fabrika's review program (experiment 65) ran live, read only, on three pull requests today's reviewer had already judged, and gave the same verdict on each: a merged pull request passed, a known fail failed on the same false sentence in a doc comment, and an open pull request passed. On the open one the reviewer used its one opened tool to file a note about something the change did not cause: the repo's list of doc places has no home for the new reports folder. The note reached the review machine as a message while the agent ran, was kept in its state, and came out beside the verdict; nothing was posted. On the known fail the program also left one more criterion open than today's reviewer did, because that criterion's proof is a ruling in the ticket's thread and the program does not read the thread. Three runs cost $1.51; a probe of the opened tool on a small model cost about a tenth of a cent.
cause: Checked: the saved verdicts of the three runs and the tool lists, which show the opened tool called once on the open pull request.
fix: A change an agent wants made is a typed input its machine opens to it, and each call is a message the machine folds into state and acts on with its own Act, so a note is never lost in a comment and a cut-off run keeps what it filed.
test: Experiment 65: the user's-job test in src/stages/review/program.test.ts, and the live table in experiments/65-review-as-a-program.md.

what: tea-fabrika's shell, tsh (experiment 67), ran review into ship on three open pull requests from one typed line, read only, in about 8 seconds and with no model: review-scripted ... | ship --mode read. Review read each pull request from GitHub and ran its gate; a scripted reviewer stood in for the agent. The two that passed went on to ship, which read them open, green, reviewed and clean and said it would put each in the merge queue; the draft was skipped by review's gate and never reached ship. Asking ship for write mode was refused at the flag before anything was read, and a pipe whose types do not fit was refused before anything started.
cause: Checked: experiments/results/67-tsh.json, from bin/tsh run as a person runs it.
fix: A stage is a program a person or a machine starts by name with typed flags, and stages wire by their types, so the driver's job is one line, checked before it runs.
test: Experiment 67: src/tsh/shell.test.ts on recorded GitHub answers, and experiments/67-tsh-real.ts on real pull requests.

what: Three rough spots in the same tsh runs. Any text fits ship's pull request input by its type as written down, so a pipe that sends plain text into ship is wired and only fails at the first value. Review needs four flags on every line, because a flag has no default. And each value a program sent was printed as one JSON line of several hundred characters; tsh now prints one short line per value and keeps the whole JSON behind --json.
cause: Checked: Effect's JSON Schema leaves out text patterns, which experiment 62 found first, and the fit check reads that JSON Schema. The flag declaration has no default field.
fix: Check fit on the schemas themselves, give flags defaults in the declaration, and let an output declare how a person reads it, with the value kept as data.
test: Experiment 67: the fit-hole test in src/tsh/shell.test.ts turns from status 1 to a refusal with status 2.

what: Experiment 69: one tsh line, operate --ship write, took a sandbox ticket (a copy of a real tea ticket, 9 criteria) through build, review, a rebuild, review again, posted verdicts and ship. Round 1's build opened a pull request; CI's API ratchet went red on a patch changeset for a new stable name; review sent it back without starting a reviewer; round 2's builder, told only that a check was red, ran the gates, found the ratchet and made the changeset minor; review passed 9 of 9; ship refused with enqueue_failed because the sandbox has no merge queue. About 29 minutes and 2 dollars, one trace of 148 spans.
cause: Checked: the tsh output, the sandbox pull request and its checks, and the Jaeger trace.
fix: The stage machines are libraries and operate is a small loop over them: review's open criteria are the next build's brief, and the loop stops when nothing is open, when a round leaves no fewer open, or at the round cap.
test: Experiment 69: src/stages/operate/program.test.ts and stop.test.ts, and the live run.

what: A kill -9 of tsh in the middle of a build left the builder (the Agent SDK's child process) running, re-parented to init, in the same working copy. The reattached run started its own builder there. The orphan was stopped by hand before the two could write over each other.
cause: Checked: ps showed the builder with parent 1 after the kill. Closing a Listen interrupts the run inside the process; a kill -9 skips that, and the child is in tsh's process group only by default.
fix: Start the builder in its own process group, killed when its Listen closes, and hold a lock on the working copy that a resumed build waits for.
test: Experiment 69's kill test, with a check that no builder is left after the kill and that a resumed build waits for the lock.

what: A tsh job told a value on its own line (operate ... ticket=X & attach %1) kept that input open after the loop ended. Nothing kept Node's event loop alive, so Node exited 13 (unsettled top-level await) and the spans not yet sent were lost. tally add=2 & attach %1 does the same. close %1 ticket after the start avoids it.
cause: Checked: reproduced with tally. A foreground call closes a value-fed input; a job does not.
fix: tsh closes an input it fed from the line once the line's values are told, for a job as for a foreground call.
test: A tsh test: tally add=2 & attach %1 ends with the total and status 0.

what: A build on sandbox ticket 3 ended stuck:no_change after 2.63 dollars. The builder used Edit three times and Write once, but the copy was clean at the end, and the loop printed nothing about why: the builder's form was in the build machine's report and the loop dropped it.
cause: Partly checked: the trace shows the edits; why the copy ended clean is not known, because the words were lost.
fix: Each loop step now carries says: the builder's summary, what it left and any problem, and for a review each open criterion.
test: src/stages/operate/program.test.ts checks says on build and review steps.

what: Experiment 69's restart: tsh was killed with kill -9 about a minute into round 2's build. tsh -c 'jobs; attach %1' found the job and went on at round 2's build, not round 1. The run ended as the first did: review passed 7 of 7, verdicts posted, ship stuck on the missing merge queue. One pull request, two commits on its branch, one review per round, no duplicate.
cause: Checked: gh on the sandbox's pull requests and the branch's commits. A test first caught a double push: the builder's Listen reopens when the kept machine loads and can move it on before resume is sent. Starters now read the kept state before the machine starts and send resume only for the phase it was kept in.
fix: Every starter reads the kept state first; one helper in tea-program would make that the only way.
test: src/stages/build/program.test.ts and src/stages/operate/program.test.ts restart cases.

what: Experiment 69b: the ship machine landed two reviewed sandbox pull requests through a real merge queue, each from one tsh line (ship-sandbox --mode write pr=<sandbox pull request>), no agent. Pull 4: enqueued 3s after the start, queue CI 7m41s on the gh-readonly-queue push, merged, ship said done 24s later; 8m43s in all. Pull 5, after pull 4 landed: the same, queue CI 7m21s, done 29s after the merge; 8m44s. Each outcome's commit is the commit GitHub put on main.
cause: Checked: gh on both pull requests (merged, queue events added then removed with reason merged), the queue runs, and the Jaeger traces (ship_facts, ship_enqueue, a 520s ship_queue Listen, ship_finish). The sandbox's CI runs on push to any branch, so the queue's own branch got the required check with no merge_group trigger.
fix: None needed for the merge path. The wait on the queue polls every 30s; that is the whole gap between the merge and the answer.
test: Re-run on any reviewed sandbox pull request: ship-sandbox --mode write, then gh pr view --json mergeCommit.

what: Both merges ended done with cleanup done, but nothing was tidied: the branches build/1 and build/2 are still on the sandbox, and the build loop's working copies are still on disk. The ship program run alone answers its tidy-up with null, and the machine reads any answer as done.
cause: Checked: src/stages/ship/handlers.ts says ship_finish does nothing for a run with no working copy; the machine maps ship_finish_ok to cleanup done.
fix: Let the tidy-up answer what it did, and say cleanup not_run when it did nothing, or give the ship run the build's working copy and branch to remove.
test: A ship machine test where ship_finish does nothing asserts cleanup is not done.

what: Experiment 71: a kill -9 of tsh now stops the builder and everything it started. Three live kills about 80s into a build, two mid command (one mid npx tsc: nine processes under tsh, the tsc chain in a process group of its own). Each time the guard, claude and every command were gone about 1s later and the copy's lock was free. A one-second ps watch never counted two builders on the copy in 1,014 reads.
cause: Checked: ps snapshots at the kill and each second after, and a flock try on the lock file. claude runs each Bash command in a session of its own, so the guard walks the tree and signals every group, and remembers what it saw under claude.
fix: The guard (src/stages/build/guard.ts): a flock on <copy>.lock held by claude itself, and a socket on fd 3 whose end tells it to stop the tree.
test: src/stages/build/guard.test.ts, and the live kill in experiments/71-builder-stops.md.

what: Experiment 71: a builder started again after a kill -9 carried its conversation on. The reattached run started claude with --resume=<the round's id>; its first words were that so far it had only read code and reproduced the error in a scratch folder; it ran git status and went on to the fix without reading those files again. It ended done and opened pull 9, runs 2. First life $0.42 and 1.3 min, resumed life $2.23 and 11.7 min. Three first lives each spent $0.42 to $0.52 reaching the same point; the resumed first turn cost $0.04.
cause: Checked: the claude argv of both lives, the conversation file, and its budget marks.
fix: The build machine keeps a session id per round; the builder runs with persistSession and resumes it when getSessionInfo finds it.
test: src/stages/build/builder.test.ts, program.test.ts, and the live run in experiments/71-builder-stops.md.

what: A build job started with 'build … ticket=X & close %1 ticket; attach %1', killed, then attached again, cannot be told its ticket: the run's record keeps the input closed ('build said closed'). A bare 'attach %1' ends the job at once and tsh drops it, so the build's kept state stays in storage with no job to reach it. It happened twice. A job started without close can be told the ticket again, and goes on.
cause: Checked: src/program/program.ts says inputs the record marks closed start closed; src/tsh/execute.ts says values told on the line are not told again.
fix: tsh tells a reattached job again the values on its first line, or keeps the job and says why it ended.
test: A tsh test: start build with close, kill, attach; the kept build goes on.

what: Experiment 70: one tsh line, operate on sandbox ticket 6, ran build, review and ship in one round and merged pull 8 through the merge queue in 18m20s for $0.50 (builder $0.29, reviewer $0.21). Its trace reads at a glance: root 'operate ticket #6', 20 spans in 5 services (tsh, operate, build, review, ship), steps named 'read ticket', 'waiting on checks', 'add to merge queue', the builder one row 'builder · 12 turns' with its turns and tools as events. Stage spans carry ticket, round, pr, short head, outcome and cost. No 'invalid parent' warning.
cause: Checked: the trace read back from Jaeger 2.21.0's API, gh on pull 8 (merged) and ticket 6 (closed). Tokens are from the trace: tokens = input not read from cache + output; billed = all input + output, with no cache-write count, so a floor. Output counts are too low (see 2026-10-17-15). The ship's tidy-up left the branch build/6 and the working copies; both removed by hand after the run.
test: src/tsh/trace.test.ts pins the tree, the names, the red ship and that the typed line reaches only the root's tsh.line.

what: Per-turn output tokens on tea's chat spans are 3 to 40 on every turn: a 12-turn builder that edited files sums to 182 output tokens, a 4-turn reviewer to 23. Spread over one row per turn the small numbers looked normal; folded onto one row the sum is plainly wrong.
cause: Not checked at the source. The numbers look like the usage at the start of each streamed message, which the Agent SDK's assistant messages carry, not the final count.
fix: tea's agentSpans takes output tokens from the result message, or from the message's final usage, not from each assistant message as it starts.

what: Experiment 74: a build job started with 'build ... ticket=X & close %1 ticket; attach %1', killed with kill -9 20s into the builder, then 'jobs; attach %1' with nothing told: the build carried on from its kept state on the same conversation, ended done with runs 2, and opened one pull request (14, one commit). tsh printed '[1] build ended: its input ticket was closed, and it finished all it held'. A watch never saw two guards in 301 one-second ticks; the guard and builder were gone within 1s of each kill. Builders cost $1.16 across tickets 10, 12 and 13.
cause: Checked: the tsh output, the watch log, the builder's own session file (one per ticket, so one conversation across both lives), and gh on pull 14. Costs and tokens are the builders' session totals: tokens = input not read from cache + output; billed = all input + output.
test: src/tsh/kill.test.ts kills a real tsh twice over three tickets with build-scripted; src/stages/build/program.test.ts and src/stages/operate/program.test.ts cover closed-input restarts.

what: A build killed twice in one round ends stuck with the reason over_budget, though its builder had spent $0.24 of $3. The real cause is MAX_RUNS = 2: a builder cut off twice is not started again. The job did end and said why; it was not stranded.
cause: Checked: src/stages/build/machine.ts, resume, ends with {kind: 'stuck', why: 'over_budget'} when run >= MAX_RUNS, with the problem 'the builder was cut off 2 times'.
fix: Name that reason cut_off, apart from over_budget.

what: Experiment 73: tsh's jobs shows one status line per pull request under a review job. Read only on sandbox pulls 9, 14 and 8 with a scripted reviewer, jobs printed '#9: sent to builder: checks red', '#14: skipped (closed)', '#8: skipped (merged)' under the one job. A scripted build over three tickets showed its queue ('#2 now, 1 waiting') and each round on its own row. After kill -9 and attach, the cut round read 'builder at work, run 2' from its kept state. No agent ran; $0.
cause: Checked: the tsh output of both runs, and src/tsh/status.test.ts and src/tsh/status-attach.test.ts, which assert the same rows.
test: src/tsh/status.test.ts (three pull requests on recorded GitHub: stuck, skipped, waiting, then done) and src/tsh/status-attach.test.ts (kill and attach).

what: A status line lags its state by one Cmd. 1.5s into a live review, jobs said 'not started' while the review was already reading pull 9 from GitHub. The phases written for a person to see, such as 'reading the pull request', are the ones that never show.
cause: Checked in @demlik/tea's commit: it sets the state, saves it, reconciles Subs, awaits the Msg's Cmds, and only then calls its listeners. A watcher hears of a state once that state's Cmds have answered.
fix: tea tells listeners when the state is set, or offers a second hook that fires then.
test: A program test that holds a Cmd open and asserts the copy's line already shows the new phase.

what: A Listen whose stream fails stops the whole run with no word. While writing a tsh test, a helper's stream failed; tea put the run into draining, every later Msg was dropped, and the copy's line froze on 'waiting on checks' with no error in tsh or the test. Reproduced on main with the same helper.
cause: Checked: tea's stopOnSubFailure drains the runtime when a Sub's stream fails; tea-program does not read or print that cause.
fix: tea-program prints the run's end cause when a Sub fails it, or tea fails done() instead of draining quietly.
test: A program test whose Listen fails, asserting the job ends with a printed cause.

what: Experiment 75b: a kept run cleared while its live copy was still open came back. The kept queue cleared itself at its end inside its own scope; the copy's next save wrote it into the run's index again, so review and ship each kept 'queue' after ending. Scripted, no agent, $0.
cause: Checked: a test that reads the run's record 50 ms after the end found the queue listed; clearing after the copy's scope closed left nothing.
fix: The queue clears after its scope closes, and a ref's clear on a live copy dies with the run's name.
test: src/stages/queue.test.ts: the queue gone and staying gone; a clear under a live copy fails the program by name.

what: Experiment 75b: ship's forget could ship an answered ask again. A kill left the answered ask on ship's kept queue; at the next start a forget cleared its run while the queue worked it again, and the work found nothing kept and started fresh.
cause: Checked: the forget test timed out with the ship machine running again under the forgotten id.
fix: Forget takes the ask off the queue first, waits for the one being worked, then clears its run and says forgot.
test: src/stages/ship/program.test.ts: an answer kept until its asker forgets it, then gone, and the same id asked again runs afresh.

what: Experiment 75b: the review to ship pipe is at least once. A review killed after it finished says passed again at the next start. Ship drops the repeat only while the pull request is still on its queue; after ship cleared the bare run, only the gate reading the pull request as merged stops a second enqueue.

what: Experiment 75c: the review to ship pipe can lose a pull request. Review's save that its work ended can land before ship has kept the value it was sent; a kill between the two loses it, review never says it again and ship never had it. This was the 75b kill test's flake seen once in 4 full runs during experiment 76: #15 reviewed once, enqueued 0 times.

A ticket piped into operate and killed before operate's queue kept it now comes again and is built, reviewed and shipped once; before, it was lost.
cause: workQueue took plain values, so an input read by a kept queue could forget the ack, and a pipe into it then kept nothing.

what: Fixes after 75d: with copies closing while others change, a change's status update could meet a close holding the view and throw, which stopped that copy and failed the run (tea's "listener": An asynchronous Effect was executed with Effect.runSync).

what: Experiment 77b: the first read fence passed the one-call probe and broke a real build. git died on an unreadable user config, tests could not spawn git at all (EPERM), and pnpm could not start the version the repo pins. 15 of tea's tests failed and 213 did not run, against 5 failures in the old fence.

what: Experiment 79: a value left unacked in a pipe's outbox, sent again at the next start into an input whose shape got stricter in between, answered bad_shape. The sender failed before main, and failed the same way at every start after; only forget cleared it.
cause: The outbox resend checked the value like a first send, so a change on the receiver's side was blamed on the sender, and the value never left the outbox.
fix: Built: at a later start a kept value the receiver no longer takes moves to deadLetters on the sender's run record with why, in one write; the rest are sent again and the sender runs on. Effect cluster's defect reply for a message that no longer decodes; AMQP and Akka dead letters.
test: src/program/inputs-over-time.test.ts (dead letter, third start resends only the good one); src/program/storage.test.ts (move in one write, stale handle moves nothing).

what: Experiment 79: a run started again under its id with other flags ran main with the new flags while its record kept the first ones. A run's mode could change from read to write partway, with machine state kept from the read start.
cause: start checked the given flags against the shape but never against the flags the record kept; tsh only avoided it by passing its job record's flags.
fix: Built: a start under a kept id must give the same flags by value; other flags are refused by the first differing flag's name before the run is opened, so nothing is fenced. Temporal's fixed workflow input and 75b's AlreadyStarted.
test: src/program/inputs-over-time.test.ts (other flags refused, record untouched; same flags in another key order start; stricter kept flags refused by name).

what: Experiment 79: a host telling a run that never reads had no limit. 100,000 tells all answered queued and held 30.7 MB of heap; 1,000,000 held 309 MB.
cause: Every input's line was an unbounded queue, and tell had no word for a full one.
fix: Built: each line holds CAPACITY (1000, Akka's bounded mailbox default). tell never waits and answers full past it; a new offer waits for room, as Effect's Queue.offer does; auto pipes, outbox resends and call's told values use offer. At a run's end the lines are shut so a waiting offer answers stopped. After: 1000 queued, the rest full, 0.4 MB.
test: src/program/inputs-over-time.test.ts (100k tells, 3000 offers to a late reader in order, auto pipe waits, call hears 3000, stop and close while waiting); experiments/79-flood.ts.

what: Experiment 79: tsh with the bound in place: 1,500 and 3,000 lines piped to stdin and a 2,500-line script file all ran. Stdin pauses on the first full and offers the rest in order; a script's lines are offered.
cause: The shell is a host that tells; without waiting it would have lost lines past 1000.
fix: Built: readline (the Node edge) pauses on full and resumes when the waiting offers finish; the close waits for the last line.
test: Manual runs of tsh on piped stdin and a script file; not yet shown that the stdin path actually hit full.

what: 80: an object with a program's fields, a blank name and a blank description, ran its main through start, call and pipe. defineProgram's refusals could be skipped by not calling it.
cause: Program was a plain interface and start never asked where the object came from.
fix: Built: Program carries a type-only mark from an unexported unique symbol, so a hand-built object does not compile; defineProgram adds each program to a module WeakSet, and start, call and pipe die before anything runs for one not in it (a spread copy). 0 existing tests changed.

what: 80: a program that read one value and returned, told five, ended {kind: ended}; four values were gone without a word. Counting the line did not help: main's read took the whole line at each pull, so the four sat in a chunk main never got to and the line said 0.
cause: No run end named what was left, and Stream.fromQueue reads every value on the line at once.
fix: Built: main reads one value per pull; Ended carries unread, a count per input with values never read, taken in the turn that shuts the lines; the run's span gets an event per input. Akka's dead-letter count; the values are not kept (AMQP DLX), since a manual input already covers not losing one.
test: src/program/unread.test.ts (5 tests).

what: 80: tsh said a background job that stopped reading early 'had nothing left to do', or with its input closed 'finished all it held', while values it was told were never read.
cause: tsh worded a job's end from the end's kind alone; the end carried nothing about its inputs.
fix: Built: tsh names the unread count: a foreground line prints '<name> ended with 5 told on n never read', a job says 'it stopped reading, with 3 told on n never read'. Exit status unchanged.

what: 104c: plan ends stuck:unchecked in 5 of 60 real runs (3 of 20 controls) on a small doc ticket. what: 139: experiment 116's TLA+ spec of the hosted lane, checked against 300 real runs of the fixed lane on fabrika's host (the ledger's log read as the spec's steps), rejected all 300. It was wrong in three places: its rows had no kind (the lane stops after a stuck row), its N was the plan's length (the lane goes on while its children say done), and it owed an EXIT that the host never sends once the lane has exited. With the three fixed, the fixed lane passes 300 of 300 and today's lane fails in exactly the 123 runs that hang (115's bug). No agent ran; stand-in children only.

It changed no code. Its run on real Stryker could not finish and it said so.

what: 159: experiment 135 rerun on GPT sol (gpt-6.1-sol, effort medium) through this repo's Codex adapter on the ChatGPT plan, 174 sorts, same cases, briefs and scoring. On the 29 real no's sonnet missed on phoenix it closed 54 of 58 answers (opus 32, sonnet 6), and all 12 easy no's. It said no to built phoenix work in 12 of 20 answers (opus 8): the extra 4 are two agent-filed security audits opus kept (#2563, #8010), closed both runs as hardening with no incident. On demlik: no wrong no, routes as opus, but 6 of 26 false folds on the controls (sonnet 1). Median 8.3 s a sort, 17.5k input and 110 output tokens; no tool ran. High effort gave the same 12 answers as medium on the sample.

what: 161: one line in the bar, "a security gap is not hardening", fixed GPT sol's two closed security tickets. 114 sorts on GPT sol (medium) through this repo's Codex adapter on the ChatGPT plan. #2563 and #8010 went to plan in all 4 answers (159: closed in all 4). Wrong no on the 10 built phoenix tickets fell from 12 of 20 to 7 of 20 (opus 8), and it cost no closes: 57 of 58 on the 29 hard real no's (159: 54). It also kept one answer of #2792, a ReDoS fix. A second line against false folds on demlik (sharing code with an open plan is not enough) moved 6 of 26 false folds to 4, but it also lost #717's one right fold.

what: 162: 30 built phoenix tickets drawn at random (seed 162) and 10 held-out built security tickets, two runs each on GPT sol (gpt-6.1-sol, medium, this repo's Codex adapter on the ChatGPT plan) with 161's security line, and on opus as 135 ran it. On the random 30, GPT sol closed 9 tickets (18 of 60 answers), opus 4 (8 of 60). Every ticket opus closed, GPT sol closed too; the 5 extra are 3 bugs or decisions read as hardening with no incident (#7894, #8057, #9196) and 2 called duplicates of a related ticket (#4087 into its epic, #8018 into a closed ticket whose fix did not hold). On the security set the line held: GPT sol closed 2 of 10 (#2013 as hardening, #6585 as a duplicate of the ticket it took over), opus 2 of 10, once each. 161's "no to built work below opus" did not hold on a fair sample. Opus cost $4.71 for 80 sorts.
cause: GPT sol applies the hardening clause and the duplicate rule to their written words; 161's 10 built tickets were too few, and half were picked for being closed.
fix: Do not move triage to GPT sol on this bar. Narrow the hardening clause (a real bug in shipped code is not hardening) and say a ticket that takes over or reopens another is not its duplicate, then rerun these 40 and the 29 hard no's.

what: 160: four real `codex app-server` jobs of one person at once, in the experimental chatgptAuthTokens mode, fed only access tokens by one login manager that holds the refresh token, against 157's fake model and token server. The access token ran out under all four at once: one refresh a round, 12 of 12 jobs right over 3 rounds, no dead login, about 12 ms added. With the manager's guards off, four refreshes at once, most with the same refresh token, killed the login and 0 of 12 finished. A refresh 12 s late stalled the job 12 s (app-server waits about 10 s, then asks again) but did not kill it. No job saw the refresh token: 0 in stdio, requests or files over 37 jobs.
cause: The manager takes a lock for each refresh and, inside it, answers with the token it already holds when that is newer than the job's. app-server's refresh ask names only the account, so the host must remember which access token it gave each job.
fix: If one Codex job per person at a time starts to hurt, run one login manager per person on their own machine or in one box with several app-servers, never in our locker (148's rule). Answer each refresh ask in under 10 s.
test: experiments/160-one-login-many-workers.ts

what: Jev's first live use, a duplicate hint when a ticket is filed, measured on this repo's own tracker: every ticket filed again against the tickets open at its filing, plus 24 hand-written paraphrases, through the shipped word filter, question and live Jev Layer. The filter kept every true pair's original among its 20.

what: A child stacked on a parent that landed squashed (532 on 520, which merged as PR 542 after more commits) showed 17 conflicts, because git's merge base predates the parent's whole branch. Merging each file three ways against the parent head the child started from (d71c573e) left 5, all small.

what: PR 545's real Stryker scenario passed on the laptop and failed in CI with ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson is not a function. Both resolve TypeScript 7.0.2. The law sets TMPDIR inside its fixture, so run.sh's empty none.json became a project file; on Linux Stryker then parsed it with TypeScript's JS API, which TypeScript 7 lacks. On macOS the temp folder sits under /var, a link to /private/var, so the path never matched and the bug hid.
cause: An empty tsconfig is still a tsconfig to Stryker once it is inside the project; the laptop's linked temp path masked it.
fix: run.sh points tsconfigFile at a path nothing writes. To reproduce a Linux-only path bug on a Mac, run the law with TMPDIR set to its real path (pwd -P).

what: Two review rounds on ticket 318's loosening check each found new source forms that hide a weaker law: first skipIf and runIf, test options, aliases, unbounded generators, shared options and removed numRuns; after the fix, aliased muting, flipped skipIf values, typed or computed options, tagged each tables, aliased expect imports and other fast-check imports. Each round's fix widened a small lexer, and the next review found the next form. The driver stopped the loop and sent the shape question to the lead.
cause: A pattern parser over test source cannot cover every way TypeScript can express the same weaker law; the review asks for the whole class, so the gap never closes by adding forms.

cause: In a dynamic language, added code in the same module can reach any old law's state, and a token lexer cannot be trusted on its own input; so no parser can prove an in-file addition harmless.
fix: Tests 9f5ab5b1 goes stricter: clear only byte-identical exam files, new regular test files with no shared-state reach, and in-place mapped title swaps judged on raw text; every other change, including new tests added to an old file, goes to the lead's hand check. what: Before writing K20 (test data from Effect's schema generators), a probe ran effect 4.1.1's Arbitrary.schema at seed 119120 on next/'s schemas. It gave up with SampleError after 2001 discards on Id.make's ids, TraceId and Dead; ProcessId, Down and Activity passed with 0 invalid values. @effect/vitest's it.prop calls Arbitrary.schema on any Schema input, so it fails the same way.

Sent to ticket 518 as its amendment A9. Upstream: https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/10479. effect 4.1.2 does not change the arbitrary code.

what: Ticket 382: Claude tests and build steps that needed the app running bounced back to the lead. The sandbox refused creating state/electron.lock, so the agent ran no capture, no Electron law and no shot, and answered send. It happened on the layers and project window lanes.
cause: drive.ts took the Electron lock outside the box only for mutation. Any other step with Electron work had to take the lock itself, and the box writes only its own folder and caches.
fix: drive.ts --electron (Claude only) takes the lock outside the box before the agent starts, holds it for the whole step, and tells the agent it is held. The sandbox profile is unchanged; a pinned law holds it byte for byte.
test: drive.test.ts: holdsElectron and the tail agree on every step and flag, the profile never names BOXES/state, the pinned profile, and --electron on Codex exits 2.

what: Today's lead tooling: box.sh gc removed no box for a day. The disk reached 98 to 99 percent, about 59 GB sat in the boxes folder and about 14 GB more in linked worktrees of merged pull requests, and drive refused five lanes for under 20 GB free. A dry run said 28 boxes were touched 0 min ago, among them p12 boxes whose lane (PR 530) merged that morning. Nobody saw it, because gc printed no keep line.
cause: gc measured a box's idle age from its git data folder and index, and its own git status writes both: it makes index.lock in the git data folder on every read, and rewrites the index when a file's stat changed. drive runs gc on every start, so no box was ever 2 h idle. Separately, catchup.sh removes only boxes on the PR's exact branch, never the lane's -wip boxes, and no tool removed a lead's or agent's linked worktree after its PR landed. Ten test processes left over by packages/pipeline's builder-stop fixture (guard.test.ts), about a day old, also hold four boxes busy.
fix: gc runs git with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and measures idle from the box folder, the index and the HEAD log's newest time stamp only (git gc's reflog expiry rewrites every worktree's HEAD log, so its file time lies too); a stuck box's 24 h hold ends once its lane merged (22 p12 boxes were held stuck after PR 530 merged); it prints every keep with its reason and the pids that hold a box; it saves a merged box's HEAD under refs/keep/box/ before removing it; it also removes clean, idle linked worktrees whose lane's pull request merged or closed. drive names gc's keeps when it still refuses on disk. Decision 0019: cleanup is the tooling's job.
test: gc.test.ts: a gc read of a box does not change when the box was last touched (fails with the old git env); decideWorktree removes only clean, idle, unlocked worktrees of a landed lane.

what: Ticket 286: P14's build (box p14-build1, Claude opus, 67 min) came back stuck:fetch_failed with not_owner on next/apps/fabrika/docs/p14/colorScheme-one.png. The approved plan gives build the folders next/apps/fabrika/docs/p14/ and next/programs/counter/docs/p14/ for the shots, and plancheck --owners-json lists each as that folder key.
cause: stepcommit and box.sh fetch looked owners up by exact path, so a folder row owned nothing. Every shot round on every lane would hit it.
fix: A key ending in / owns every path under it, the longest such row winning; a path with an empty, '.' or '..' part gets no folder owner, and a plain string prefix (owned.ts, owned.tsx) still owns nothing. Same lookup in stepcommit.sh and box.sh fetch. Ticket 436.
test: stepcommit.test.ts 'K4 a row ending in / owns every file under it, and nothing beside it': under and deeper files sign, docs/shotsx/ and a '..' escape are refused. It fails on the old exact-only lookup (checked by hand).

what: Today's lead tooling and next/ tests: ticket 381's slow law in next/apps/fabrika/src/local-stage.test.ts spent about 85% of its time in fsync. Each stage start took about 62 ms, about 13 fsyncs of about 4.5 ms in the brain outbox's durableWrite; with them skipped a start took about 9 ms. The law dropped from about 3 s to about 0.4 s and now passes Stryker's dry run (340 ms). On the way the Codex tests step answered stuck because its sandbox cannot run pgrep, so it skipped pnpm typecheck; the lead ran it outside (green). The mutation step then waited about 65 minutes on state/electron.lock held by another session's e2e run at 0% CPU.
cause: The law ran the real Node FileSystem, so every durable write waited on the disk. The tests brief told the agent to wait on pgrep before typecheck, which the box cannot run. The Electron lock has no holder timeout.
fix: The law gets Node's real FileSystem with each opened File's sync as Effect.void; seed, runs and assertions unchanged; the outbox's own law still pins the sync calls. Lead runs typecheck outside a Codex box when the box cannot pgrep.
test: Mutation arm a vs arm b on seed 119120: narrowing none; the sample missed stage.ts and local-stage.ts (follow-up ticket filed).

what: Ticket 341, today's lead tooling on today's agents package: the first real lane under chain.ts on the Agent interface over ACP (PR 691). Lane t411 from its mutation step: the box, the plan in the prompt, the git view and the sampler worked (54 mutants chosen), then Stryker could not start, listen EPERM on 0.0.0.0. The step answered stuck in 1.9 minutes for $0.19 list. The chain asked its judgment turn (read-only Codex row, $0.17 list, 12 seconds), which parked the lane for the lead. Exit 20, nothing changed in the main checkout, the stuck box kept. No full lane has run on the new path.
cause: The Claude ACP row's sandbox has no local port binding and no unix sockets, and the Codex rows refuse listen too. Before PR 691 the mutation step ran on claude -p under drive's own profile, which allowed it.
fix: A harness row, or a turn's limits, that opens local binding with outbound network still closed (ticket 483). Until then PR 691 stays a draft: landed, it would stop every lane's mutation step.
test: Run lane t411 from --start mutation again on that row: Stryker's dry run passes and at least one mutant gets a real result.

what: Ticket 341, today's lead tooling: four things the Agent interface's containment broke in drive.ts and chain.ts before the lane could start, each found by reading the harness and three smoke turns ($0.60 list together). 1. A box reads nothing beside itself, so a step could not read the approved plan kept beside the boxes, and the judgment could not read the state file or the report. 2. git did not work in a box at all: its data is beside the box and borrows objects from the main checkout, both closed, so the mutation sampler's git diff and a review's diff had nothing. 3. The chain told the mutation step BUILD=a..b, and the sampler diffs BUILD^ against BUILD. 4. On the read-only Codex row one refused writing command ended the turn cancelled with no answer (ticket 484). Also measured: the Codex fence table for a box among 3,053 names is 129 lines of 600, so it fits; and the Codex row's token count grew about 25,000 a request, so it looks like a turn total, not the last request (ticket 485).
cause: PR 691 swapped the agent start onto the harness rows and was proven by one-turn smokes in a temp folder, which need no plan, no git and no socket.
fix: In PR 691: drive puts the plan's text in the prompt, chain puts the state file's tail and the report in the judgment's prompt and runs it on the read-only row, drive gives each box a git view (a hard-linked mirror of the main checkout's git data, holding the box as a linked worktree, which the harness opens read-only) and removes it when the step ends, BUILD is the newest build commit, and a review is told to run no writing command.
test: The lane's own run: the sampler read its diff through the view and chose 54 mutants; the judgment answered from the prompt alone.

what: Experiment 248, next/: the first run of the record wire laws on the ported RecordPart failed 10 of 10 with ControlError unreachable and no cause. The cause was a binding name: Alchemy's runtime reads env[<class name>], and the stack bound the class as RECORD. Finding it took four runs with a temporary console line, because platform.ts and control.ts turn every cause into unreachable and the stage's log stays empty.
cause: The hand-written clients map any rejected call to LedgerError unreachable and drop the cause; the control socket answers only the reason word.
fix: Keep the cause on the failed call as a span attribute or a log line the stage keeps, so the first failed run names it. Alchemy's typed stub does carry it (RpcCallError has cause), so the port removes most of this.
test: Plant a wrong binding name on a ported object and read the stage's log: the class name must be in it after one run.

what: Today's lead tooling: the leak check's new rule (an added line that only respaces a removed line of its file is old text, PR 709) was measured on ticket 466's held format sweep, as its working copy stood that day. Main's check gave 72 hits; the new one gives 28. Of the 28, 17 are lines whose only change is a space put inside braces, which collapsing runs of spaces does not cover, and 11 are lines the 120-column setting wrapped another way, which no line-by-line rule can pair. So the sweep is still held. Trying the wider rule on a copy of the script (also ignore a space just inside a brace) left 11.
cause: The owner's yes covered whitespace runs and one last ; or ,. Deleting whitespace, or ignoring brace spacing, was not shown to be safe, so neither is in the pull request.
fix: One yes or no from the owner on also ignoring a space just inside a brace, with its own edge case list; the 11 rewrapped lines need a hand edit either way.
test: Run the leak check on the sweep's diff again after the call and count the hits.
